Body Composition Analysis

Dieting hard but the scale won't move? Or a "normal" weight but still unhappy with your shape? A body composition analysis goes beyond the scale. In about a minute, the InBody test measures your body fat, muscle, hidden visceral fat and water balance. Our doctors then turn those numbers into a plan that targets fat, protects muscle and shows real progress.

~1 minTest time
No needlesPainless
15+Measurements
4–8 weeksRetest
Book Now See what it measures
On this pageOverviewYour reportCheck your numbersFind your planBody typesHow to prepareProcessScale vs BMIFAQs

Overview

What is Body Composition Analysis?

Your weight is made up of fat, muscle, water and bone. A normal scale lumps them all into one number, so it can't tell you whether you've lost fat or muscle, or whether that extra kilo is water.

A body composition analysis, often called an InBody test, measures each part separately. You stand barefoot on the machine and hold its handles for about a minute while a tiny, painless signal passes through your body. You get a detailed report showing your body fat percentage, skeletal muscle, visceral fat, body water, metabolic rate and a breakdown for each arm, leg and the trunk.

Read more: how the test works

Muscle holds a lot of water, so electricity flows through it easily. Fat holds very little water, so it resists the signal. By sending a very small current at several frequencies and measuring the resistance, the analyser works out how much fat, muscle and water you have, and where it is.

Because the test is quick, painless and repeatable, it's ideal for tracking your progress every few weeks.

1. MeasureStand on the analyser for about a minute.
2. UnderstandOur doctor explains your fat, muscle and visceral fat.
3. ActGet a plan built on your numbers, and retest to track progress.

Your report

What Your Body Composition Report Shows

Tap each row of this sample report to see what it means, the healthy range and why it matters.

Sample reportFor illustration only

Tap a row to see what it means.

Body fat percentage

What it is: The share of your weight that's fat. It tells you far more than weight or BMI alone.

Why it matters: High body fat raises the risk of diabetes, heart disease, PCOS and joint pain, even at a "normal" weight.

Healthy guideMen: about 10–20% · Women: about 18–28%

Skeletal muscle mass

What it is: The muscle you use to move. It burns calories even at rest and protects your joints and blood sugar.

Why it matters: Low muscle slows your metabolism and makes weight harder to lose and keep off. Crash diets often lose muscle, not fat.

Healthy guideCompared with the healthy range for your height and sex

Visceral fat level

What it is: The hidden fat wrapped around your organs inside the tummy, not the fat you can pinch.

Why it matters: Visceral fat is strongly linked to diabetes, fatty liver, high blood pressure and heart disease. Many slim-looking people still have high levels.

Healthy guideBelow 10 is healthy · 10 or above needs action

Body water balance

What it is: How much water is in your body, and the balance between water inside and outside your cells.

Why it matters: A high ratio can point to swelling, inflammation or water retention, and helps your doctor spot hidden problems.

Healthy guideECW/TBW ratio about 0.360–0.390

Basal metabolic rate

What it is: The calories your body burns at rest, just to keep you alive.

Why it matters: Knowing your BMR helps us set a realistic calorie target, so you lose fat without starving.

Healthy guideDepends on your muscle mass

Segmental analysis

What it is: Muscle and fat measured separately in each arm, each leg and the trunk.

Why it matters: Shows imbalances, weak areas and where fat is stored, so your exercise plan targets the right places.

Healthy guideLeft and right should be balanced

What to expect

Benefits of Body Composition Analysis

Clear numbers that turn guesswork into a plan.

Beyond the Scale

Separates fat, muscle and water instead of giving one number.

Finds Hidden Fat

Measures visceral fat around your organs, the most harmful kind.

Protects Your Muscle

Shows if you're losing fat or muscle, so your plan can be adjusted.

Takes About a Minute

Stand on the machine, hold the handles, done. No needles.

A Plan Built on Data

Your calorie target, diet and exercise plan are set from your own numbers.

Water Balance

Checks for water retention and swelling that the scale can't explain.

Safe and Painless

Uses a tiny, harmless electrical signal you can't feel.

Tracks Real Progress

Repeat tests every 4 to 8 weeks show exactly what's changing.

Swipe to see more

Problems it solves

Why the Scale Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

Tap a situation that sounds like you.

"I'm dieting but the scale won't move."
You may be losing fat and gaining muscle or water at the same time. Your report shows the real change, so you don't give up on a plan that's working.
"My weight is normal but I still have a tummy."
This is often called "skinny fat": normal weight with high body fat and low muscle. Only body composition analysis can spot it.
"I lost weight fast, then put it all back on."
Crash diets often burn muscle, which slows your metabolism. Tracking muscle helps you lose fat while keeping your metabolism strong.
"I have PCOS or thyroid problems."
Hormones change where you store fat and how much water you hold. Your report helps your doctor plan treatment around them.
"My blood sugar or cholesterol is high."
High visceral fat is a key driver. Measuring it gives you and your doctor a clear target to bring down.
"I train hard but don't see results."
Segmental analysis shows muscle in each limb, so you can fix weak spots and imbalances.

Who it's for

Who Should Get Tested?

  • Anyone starting a weight-loss or fitness plan
  • People with PCOS, thyroid problems or diabetes
  • Anyone on weight-loss injections or a medical weight plan
  • People with a normal weight but a big tummy
  • Athletes and gym-goers tracking muscle
  • Anyone who wants a health check beyond the scale

Not suitable if you

  • Have a pacemaker or implanted electronic device
  • Are pregnant

Body types

C-, I- or D-Shape: What's Your Body Type?

Your report compares your weight, muscle and fat. The pattern they make shows your body type and what to focus on.

C-shape

Body fat is higher than muscle. Common in people who have dieted without exercise, even if their weight looks normal.

Best for: fat loss and muscle building
Downtime: —
Sessions: focus: protein and strength work

I-shape

Weight, muscle and fat are roughly balanced. A good base to improve from.

Best for: steady fat loss or toning
Downtime: —
Sessions: focus: consistency

D-shape

Muscle is higher than average compared with fat. Typical of active, athletic people.

Best for: maintaining and fine-tuning
Downtime: —
Sessions: focus: performance

Swipe to see more

How to prepare

Get the Most Accurate Results

Small things like food, water and exercise can change your numbers, so follow these simple steps.

Do

  • Come 2 to 3 hours after your last meal
  • Use the toilet just before
  • Wear light clothes
  • Test at the same time of day each time

Avoid

  • Exercise or a sauna before the test
  • Coffee, tea and alcohol
  • A shower just before
  • Testing during your period, if you can

Bring

  • Your previous reports, if any
  • Recent blood test results
  • A list of your medicines

Remove

  • Socks and shoes
  • Watches, rings and jewellery
  • Phones and metal items from pockets

How often

  • Every 4 to 8 weeks while working on your goals
  • Same time of day and same preparation
  • Compare trends, not single numbers

What to look for

  • Body fat going down
  • Muscle staying the same or going up
  • Visceral fat dropping below 10

Your appointment

How the Body Composition Test Works

A short chat about your goals and health.

  • We note your age, height, health conditions and medicines.
  • We check that you don't have a pacemaker or implanted device.
  • You remove socks, shoes and metal items.

The test itself takes about a minute.

  • Stand barefoot on the analyser's footplates.
  • Hold the hand electrodes with your arms slightly away from your body.
  • Stay still while the machine measures.
  • You won't feel anything.

Your doctor explains your report.

  • We go through your fat, muscle, visceral fat and water balance.
  • You get your printed report to keep.
  • We set clear targets and next steps.
  • We plan your next test in 4 to 8 weeks.

Questions

Body Composition Analysis FAQs

What is a body composition analysis?
It's a quick, painless test that measures what your body is made of: fat, muscle, water and bone minerals. Unlike a normal scale, it shows how much of your weight is fat and how much is muscle, plus your hidden visceral fat.
What is an InBody test?
InBody is a widely used body composition analyser. You stand barefoot on the machine and hold the handles while a tiny, harmless electrical signal measures your body. It takes about a minute and prints a detailed report.
How does it work?
Fat, muscle and water conduct electricity differently. The machine sends a very small current through your body at several frequencies and measures the resistance to work out your fat, muscle and water, including separately for each arm, leg and the trunk.
Does the test hurt?
No. You can't feel the signal at all. It's as simple as standing on a scale.
How long does it take?
The measurement takes about a minute. With the doctor's explanation of your report, plan around 15 to 20 minutes.
How should I prepare?
Don't eat for 2 to 3 hours before, skip exercise and caffeine beforehand, empty your bladder, and remove socks, jewellery and metal. Wear light clothing.
Is it better than BMI?
Yes. BMI only uses height and weight, so it can call a muscular person overweight or miss a slim person with high body fat. Body composition analysis measures fat and muscle directly.
What is visceral fat and why does it matter?
Visceral fat is stored deep inside the tummy around your organs. It's linked to diabetes, fatty liver, high blood pressure and heart disease. A level below 10 is generally considered healthy.
What is a healthy body fat percentage?
As a general guide, about 10 to 20% for men and 18 to 28% for women. Your doctor will explain what's right for your age and goals.
How often should I get tested?
Every 4 to 8 weeks is ideal while you're working on your weight or fitness. Testing more often won't show meaningful changes.
Who should not take the test?
People with a pacemaker or other implanted electronic device shouldn't take it. It's also usually avoided during pregnancy.
Can it help with PCOS or thyroid problems?
Yes. It shows how your fat, muscle and water are changing, which helps doctors plan and track treatment for hormone-related weight gain.
Will I get a copy of my report?
Yes. You'll get your printed report, and our doctor will explain every number and what to do next.
Where can I get a body composition test in Kerala?
Facelit offers InBody body composition analysis as part of our weight management services. Contact us to book at your nearest clinic.
